name: Improper Input Validation
principle: The product receives input but does not validate required properties such as length, range, type, syntax, consistency, or authenticity before processing it. Unexpected input can drive unsafe memory access, resource consumption, control flow changes, or command execution.
detection_signals: atoi/atol/strtol/Integer.parseInt result used as size, count, index, offset, loop bound, or allocation size without lower-bound and upper-bound checks
memcpy/memmove/strncpy/read/write/malloc/new/vector::resize/Arrays.copyOf called with externally derived length not range-checked
array[index]/pointer+offset/List.get(index)/ByteBuffer.position/ByteBuffer.limit called with externally derived index or offset not bounds-checked
validation checks only null, empty, EOF, or parse success but not range, sign, missing fields, extra fields, or cross-field consistency
input decoded, concatenated, normalized, or arithmetic-derived after validation with no validation of the final value
client-side JavaScript or UI validation exists but server-side C/C++/Java handler uses the same field without validation
negative_signals: guard like if (len >= 0 && len <= MAX) dominates all uses of len as size, count, index, or offset
strtol/strtoul checks end pointer, errno overflow, sign, and accepted range before cast or use
Java code applies allowlist regex and parsed numeric range check before get/substring/allocate/copy use
server-side handler validates request.getParameter/body/header values even when client-side validation exists
URL/HTML/Unicode decoding or canonicalization occurs before allowlist validation, with no later decode before use
combined or derived values are revalidated after concatenation, arithmetic, or metadata/raw-data reconciliation
false_defense_traps: Denylist filters for bad characters without an allowlist grammar and range checks
Checking only an upper bound while negative values are possible
Validating individual fields before concatenation but not validating the combined value
Validating encoded input before URL/HTML/Unicode decoding or canonicalization
verification_focus: Does every untrusted or externally derived input have required type, syntax, range, length, consistency, and canonical form checked before security-sensitive use?

consequence_chains.trigger: unchecked input participates in arithmetic that controls loop termination
consequence_chains.consequence: integer overflow followed by infinite loop or denial of service

consequence_chains.trigger: unchecked input controls write offset or copy length
consequence_chains.consequence: out-of-bounds write and possible code execution

consequence_chains.trigger: unchecked input controls read offset or length
unchecked input controls allocation size or operation count

patch_principle: Identify all trust-boundary inputs: parameters, headers, cookies, files, filenames, environment variables, network data, database results, and API-returned data.
Canonicalize or decode input once into the internal representation before validation.
Use accept-known-good validation for type, syntax, length, range, required fields, extra fields, and cross-field business rules.
Validate derived and combined values after parsing, arithmetic, concatenation, or metadata/raw-data reconciliation.
Reject invalid input before use; do not rely only on denylists or client-side checks.

minimal_examples.vuln: int len = atoi(argv[1]); memcpy(dst, src, len);
minimal_examples.safe: char *e; long len = strtol(argv[1], &e, 10); if (*e || len < 0 || len > (long)sizeof dst) reject(); else memcpy(dst, src, (size_t)len);
